Messages.Author: John Whelan
Messages.Body:
I am curious as to how the limitations in that old Wallpaper card
Concealed Weapon would be interpretted in certain situations, these
limitations being "weapon cannot cost more than 2 pool or do more than 4
damage".

If Black Cat were given obfuscate, could she use CW to get a combat
shotgun, since it costs her only 2 pool?

If a minion already has +2 hand damage, can he use CW to equip with Bang
Nakh (giving him a total of 5 hand damage)?

If a weapon existed that inflicted +4 hand damage, would one be able to
play it with CW if ones hand damage were 0? Or could it be played
regardless of the base damage of the minion playing it?

These questions are totally pointless, of course.

Lupus Australis

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
In article <slrn6iodli....@amanda.dorsai.org>,

jbwh...@dorsai.org (John Whelan) wrote:
>
> I am curious as to how the limitations in that old Wallpaper card
> Concealed Weapon would be interpretted in certain situations, these
> limitations being "weapon cannot cost more than 2 pool or do more than 4
> damage".
>
> If Black Cat were given obfuscate, could she use CW to get a combat
> shotgun, since it costs her only 2 pool?

Yes.

> If a minion already has +2 hand damage, can he use CW to equip with Bang
> Nakh (giving him a total of 5 hand damage)?

Precedent set by a ruling on Illegal Search and Seizure: yes.
The Bang Nahk, at +2 hand damage, is viewed as a weapon that
does 2 damage by the Rules Team.

> If a weapon existed that inflicted +4 hand damage, would one be able to
> play it with CW if ones hand damage were 0? Or could it be played
> regardless of the base damage of the minion playing it?

It could be played by a vampire regardless of his base hand damage, as
above, yes (provided it didn't cost more than 2 pool, which is unlikely
unless the weapon carried a severe penalty of its own).
